records.name: Marina Van Bos
records.bio: Van Bos is named among the IRPA analysts who examined glass, adhesives and paint layers in the Liège Blaschka collection. The analysis forms part of the evidence base for the collection’s conservation and exhibition history.

records.name: Andrew Dickson White
records.bio: White’s papers form one of the archival contexts through which Cornell’s early natural-history collecting and institutional networks can be reconstructed. The project keeps him as an institutional actor where Blaschka-related correspondence or collection formation intersects that archive.
records.open: His precise object-level role in Cornell’s Blaschka acquisitions should be distinguished from the broader institutional context preserved in his papers.

records.name: Louis Agassiz
records.roles: zoologist · Harvard museum founder · Ward correspondent
records.bio: A surviving 1869 letter from Henry Augustus Ward to Agassiz places the Museum of Comparative Zoology founder in the early Ward–Harvard institutional network. The finding-aid evidence establishes correspondence but does not by itself prove that this particular letter concerned Blaschka models.
records.open: The 1869 Ward–Agassiz letter still requires content-level verification before it can be treated as Blaschka correspondence.

records.name: Elizabeth Hodges Clark
records.roles: Harvard museum worker · receiving and inspection
records.bio: Harvard historical interpretation identifies Clark as likely assisting with unpacking and inspecting Blaschka invertebrates and flowers. The project retains that labour history while marking the attribution as institutional interpretation rather than item-level documentary proof.
records.open: The unpacking and inspection role is probable rather than object-by-object documented.

records.name: Jan Brazier
records.bio: Brazier co-authored the reconstruction of model and wall-chart circulation for teaching biology in Australia and New Zealand. The study is especially useful for the Frič–Liversidge network, museum consignments and the later University of Sydney teaching loan.

records.name: Molly Duggins
records.bio: Duggins co-authored the reconstruction of teaching models and wall charts in Australia and New Zealand. Her work supplies a broader material and educational context for the Blaschka models entering Australasian museums through Frič and related dealers.

records.name: Deborah White
records.roles: museum writer · Australian Museum conservation history
records.bio: White documented the restoration challenges surrounding the Australian Museum’s Blaschka sea anemones and their return to display in March 2010 after many decades. Her account provides an institutional anchor for the collection’s recent material history.

records.name: W. J. Stephens
records.roles: university scientist · Australian Museum loan actor
records.bio: Stephens appears in the 1884 transfer of the Frič teaching collection from the Australian Museum to the University of Sydney for lecture use. The wider collection context is relevant to Blaschka circulation, although the surviving evidence does not isolate which Blaschka objects, if any, were included in that particular loan.
records.open: The Blaschka object scope of the 1884 loan remains unresolved.

records.name: Michela Mitchell
records.bio: Mitchell participated in the Australian Museum’s 2009 identification campaign with Patricia Egan and Chris Meechan. The team compared underside number stickers with the 1871 catalogue and published zoological illustrations, identifying all but one surviving model.

records.name: Sabine Hackethal
records.bio: Hackethal authored the institutional history used to reconstruct the Berlin Blaschka collection: its acquisition scale, surviving pieces, present locations, Schulze collaboration and continuing teaching use. The account accompanied the 2012 Berlin exhibition.
